$comment: PACKAGE DEPENDENCY TABLE (#1625, epic #1621).
Which workspace packages consume which. The CI change classifier derives
its job fan-out from this: if a package changes, every job whose package
TRANSITIVELY depends on it must run too, or a change can break a consumer
whose suite never ran on the pull request that broke it.
This is a DIFFERENT question from .github/root-guard-ownership.json, and
the two are kept apart on purpose:
root-guard-ownership.json -- SOURCE OWNERSHIP. Which job validates a
given file. Answers 'who checks this?'
package-dependencies.json -- BUILD/TEST PROPAGATION. Which packages are
broken by a change to another package. Answers 'who else must re-run?'
A guard file has an owner but no dependents; a package has dependents but
no owner in that sense. Merging them would force one of the two questions
to be answered in the other's vocabulary.
FIELDS
dependsOn  Job flags of the packages this one consumes DIRECTLY. The
classifier computes the transitive closure itself, so never
pre-expand a chain here -- write what package.json declares
and nothing more.
note       Anything a reader would otherwise have to rediscover.
Keys are OUTPUT FLAGS, not directory names: packages/mcp-server is the
`mcp_server` flag. Only packages that have a CI job of their own appear.
packages/core and packages/qa-agent deliberately do not: neither has a job,
and both fall to the packages/* catch-all that forces the full matrix. That
is over-routing rather than under-routing, and is pinned as a RETAINED row
in scripts/ci/routing-matrix.mjs for #1626 to decide on.
CHECKED, NOT DECLARED. scripts/ci/package-dependencies.test.mjs reads every
package.json and fails if this table disagrees with the real @haven_ai/*
dependencies -- in both directions. devDependencies count: packages/mcp-server
only uses @haven_ai/signer in its tests, and its tests are exactly what its
CI job runs.
NOT a completeness claim about jobs. Whether every package HAS a job, and
whether every job is reachable, is #1626.
EXCEPTION: `noOwnJob` (#2996). scripts/ci/package-dependencies.test.mjs also
scans every packages/*/package.json on disk for a `test` script and fails if
the workspace has neither an entry in `packages` above nor a listed reason
here -- the gap #2996 found: packages/demo-merchant-mcp had 142 tests and a
`test` script, and nothing in this table, .github/workflows/ci.yml, or this
manifest ever noticed. Add a package here ONLY when leaving it un-run is a
deliberate, stated choice with the follow-up that removes it named in the
reason (core and qa-agent today, see #3005) -- never
as a way to silence this check.

noOwnJob.core: Shared kernel with no job of its own. A core change routes to the full matrix, but NO job runs `npm run test -w packages/core` — its 3 test files (incl. the DEFAULT_CHAIN_ID guard) do not run in CI today. Exempted so this pin stays honest, not because the gap is acceptable: #3005 adds the job and removes this entry.
noOwnJob.qa-agent: Private workspace; its `vitest run` (24 test files) runs in NO workflow — qa-dev.yml runs the live scenario runner, not the unit tests. Exempted so this pin stays honest: #3005 adds a unit-test job and removes this entry.

frontend.note: Consumes @haven_ai/core, which has no job flag, so there is nothing to fan out to. A core change forces the full matrix by the packages/* catch-all instead.

backend.note: Also consumes @haven_ai/core; same as frontend, core carries no job flag.

sdk.note: The root of the graph. Nothing internal is below it, which is why an SDK change fans out the widest.

connect.note: The connector bundles the MCP runtime and the signer it hands out, so it rebuilds when either moves.

mcp_server.note: @haven_ai/signer and @haven_ai/mcp are devDependencies, consumed by src/hosted-signer-integration.test.ts and src/strict-tool-input.test.ts. mcp_server_checks runs those tests, so both dependencies are real for CI even though neither is shipped -- the mcp edge (#2348) exists so a rename in packages/mcp's toolSchemas fans out here, which is precisely what that test pins.

cli.note: Declares no internal dependencies at all, which is why an SDK change does not fan out to it.

demo_merchant.note: packages/demo-merchant-mcp (#2996). Declares no @haven_ai/* dependency today -- checked, not assumed: it does not import @haven_ai/sdk or any sibling package, so an SDK change does not fan out to it. If it starts consuming one, package-dependencies.test.mjs's real-manifest check catches the mismatch.
